questions.question_text: Where should one pair of brackets go to make $3+7 \times 5=50$ true?

options.why: Groups the multiplication already done first, leaving the value as $38$.
Groups the entire expression but does not change which inner operation happens first.

questions.question_text: Where should one pair of brackets go to make $28-12 \div 4=4$ true?

options.why: Groups the division already done first, so the value remains $25$.
Enclosing the complete expression does not change its internal operation order.

questions.question_text: In $15 \times (11-7)+6$, which calculation must be performed first?

options.why: Starts multiplication before completing the operation inside the brackets.
Groups terms on opposite sides of a bracket that are not grouped together.
Combines separate outside terms and ignores both multiplication and brackets.

questions.question_text: Where should one pair of brackets go to make $5+3 \times 4=32$ true?

options.why: Groups the multiplication already done first, giving $17$ instead of $32$.
Encloses the complete expression without changing its internal operation order, giving $17$ instead of $32$.
Divides $90$ by $8$ before using the brackets, then adds $2+7$.
Pulls the outside $+7$ into the divisor and calculates $90 \div (8+2+7)$.
Keeps multiplication first and gives $37$, so it does not reach the target.
Groups the final difference and gives $21$, not the required value.
Uses two bracket pairs and changes the value to $32$ rather than $92$.
